segments.text: Morgan has a plausible Harbor proposal. Add a free digital skills session next
month. The room note is current. The attendance note suggests interest. The
facilitator is still available for review, not confirmed. A colleague suggests
paying for a small printing run to test flyers. The amount sounds minor. Morgan
stops at the word paying. A recommendation can sit in the brief. A
purchase needs a separate human decision. The same paper workflow now
has two questions. Should Harbor propose the session and should anyone authorize
a specific expense? Chapter 17's spend envelope names amount, counterparty,
purpose, execution window, retry limit, trace, and approval. The workbook adds
currency, requesting role, forbidden actions, and revocation. In the Harbor case,
use a proposed $40 print test with the course printer and a two-day window. The
number is classroom arithmetic, not a quote, budget, or authorization. The
envelope is incomplete until the actual approving human can see the evidence and
exact terms. It cannot be stretched into a recurring charge or an up-to range.
Harbor's preparation role has no payment authority. It may draft a spend
request. It cannot place an order, enter a card, increase a cap, or trigger paid
API usage. Put a closed gate between the proposed envelope and any dollar
moving verb. If the cost, vendor, window, or evidence changes, the paper envelope
goes back to Morgan. If it expires, it stays closed. A prior approval of the
session idea would not approve the print order. The approval has to match the
action. Now write the decision Morgan actually owns. Chapter 18 uses five
sections. Context, options, recommendation, reversibility, and what would change our
mind. Option A is to propose a session subject to facilitator confirmation. Option
B is to hold the proposal and gather a fresh staffing commitment. Give B a fair
case. It protects Harbor from promising a session it cannot staff. The
recommendation can favor A only if the brief clearly carries that condition.
Morgan can also choose hold. The agent's framing must leave room for
disagreement. Put the spend question on its own line. Even if Morgan favors a
conditional session proposal, the print request remains held. The brief should
name Morgan as decision owner, the course deadline, the evidence gap, and what can
be reversed. A draft brief can be withdrawn. A flier sent into the community
cannot be pulled back with the same ease. That difference is why preparation
and side effects have different gates. An honest decision brief makes the
strongest alternative visible and tells the reviewer what evidence would
overturn the recommendation. Pause. Which sentence in the brief would stop
available for review from becoming confirmed? Fill a spend envelope, then a
decision brief. Give the envelope an exact illustrative amount named course
counterparty, purpose, window, one or zero retry limit, trace, human approver, and
revocation condition. Market unapproved. Give the brief two real options. A fair
case for the rejected option, a recommendation, reversibility, evidence gap,
and a hold outcome. Keep the facilitator unconfirmed. Use a fictional or approved
example. Do not use private operational data, open a checkout, use a card, call a
provider, or publish a session. Save revision 10 as a draft. Morgan has two
distinct decisions and the evidence for both. Neither has been exercised. Next,
we will make the pending work visible without turning a phone notification into
a second control room.
